title: TC Synchronization and Channel Coding
issue: Recommended Standard, Issue 4 (Blue Book), with Editorial Change 1 (October 2024)
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) lists 231.0-B-1 (September 2003), B-2 (September 2010) and B-3 (September 2017) as superseded and 231.0-B-4 (July 2021) as the 'Current issue'. Issue 4 clarifies the procedures for the short LDPC codes and adds support for USLP. EC 1 (October 2024) corrects the figure listing in the table of contents and changes the page size to A4.
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **TC Synchronization and Channel Coding Sublayer**, the uplink counterpart of [TM coding](../ccsds/tm-coding.md). It takes variable-length [TC](../ccsds/tc-sdlp.md) or [USLP](../ccsds/uslp.md) Transfer Frames, protects them with error-control coding, wraps them in a **Communications Link Transmission Unit (CLTU)** and hands them to the Physical Layer through a Physical Layer Operations Procedure (PLOP). It is the specification behind every telecommand decoder on board and behind the CLTUs a ground station radiates, including those delivered through [SLE FCLTU](../ccsds/sle/fcltu.md). The rationale and worked examples are in [230.1-G-3](ccsds-230-1-230x1g3e1.md).

Section 2 lists four functions: error-control coding, synchronization, optional pseudo-randomizing and optional repeated transmissions. Section 3 defines the modified (63,56) BCH code with generator g(x) = x^7+x^6+x^2+1, which gives 64-bit codewords of 56 information bits, 7 inverted parity bits and a zero filler bit, padded with alternating-bit fill. It can be decoded in error-detecting or error-correcting mode. Section 4 defines the rate-1/2 (128,64) and (512,256) LDPC codes through their parity-check and circulant generator matrices. Section 5 defines the CLTU: Start Sequence (16-bit 0xEB90 for BCH, 64-bit 0x034776C7272895B0 for LDPC), codewords and Tail Sequence (C5C5 C5C5 C5C5 C579 for BCH, an optional 128-bit pattern for LDPC (128,64), none for (512,256)). It also gives the receiver state machine with states S1 Inactive, S2 Search and S3 Decode and events E1 to E5. Section 6 specifies the Bit Transition Generator randomizer, h(x) = x^8+x^6+x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1, which is optional with BCH and mandatory with LDPC. Section 7 specifies the carrier modulation modes CMM-1 to CMM-4 and PLOP-1 and PLOP-2, and section 8 the managed parameters. Annex A gives the ChannelAccess service with its optional Repetitions parameter.

contents.title: Managed Parameters for BCH and LDPC Coding

key_points.text: Issue 4 (July 2021) clarifies the short-LDPC procedures and adds USLP support; EC 1 (October 2024) fixes the table of contents and moves to A4.
Four sublayer functions: error-control coding, synchronization, pseudo-randomizing (optional) and repeated transmissions (optional).
The modified BCH code can be decoded in error-detecting or error-correcting mode; the FECF of the TC or USLP frame can lower the undetected-error probability, especially in error-correcting mode.
Repeated transmission is requested with an optional Repetitions parameter in the service primitive; how the repetitions are performed is not specified.
BCH codeword: 56 information bits plus 7 parity bits from g(x) = x^7 + x^6 + x^2 + 1 plus a filler bit that is always zero, 64 bits (8 octets) in total.
Two rate-1/2 LDPC codes are specified, (n=128, k=64) and (n=512, k=256), built from M x M circulant submatrices with M = k/4.
CLTU = Start Sequence + encoded codewords + Tail Sequence. For BCH, the Start Sequence is 16 bits (0xEB90) and the Tail Sequence is 64 bits (C5C5 C5C5 C5C5 C579).

For LDPC, the Start Sequence is 64 bits (0347 76C7 2728 95B0); an optional 128-bit Tail Sequence (5555 5556 AAAA AAAA 5555 5555 5555 5555) applies only to LDPC (128,64), and no tail is used with (512,256).

CLTU reception states are S1 INACTIVE, S2 SEARCH and S3 DECODE; events E1 to E5 are channel activation, channel deactivation, start sequence found, codeword rejection and (for LDPC 128,64) tail sequence detected.

The randomizer polynomial is h(x) = x^8 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1, starting from all ones; randomization is always applied with LDPC and required with BCH unless proper operation without it is verified.
With BCH the BTG is preset at the start of the Transfer Frame(s); with LDPC it is preset at the start of each codeword and reset after each codeword.
PLOP-2 shall be used for missions whose planning begins after September 2010; the preferred minimum Acquisition Sequence length is 16 octets.
Carrier Modulation Modes: CMM-1 unmodulated carrier, CMM-2 carrier with acquisition sequence, CMM-3 carrier with CLTU, CMM-4 carrier with idle sequence.

Managed parameters: code type (BCH or LDPC), maximum CLTU length, maximum Repetitions, PLOP-1 or PLOP-2; for BCH also the decoding mode, allowed errors in the Start Sequence (0 or 1) and randomizer use; for LDPC the code length and use of the tail sequence.

notes: The slug's 'e1' is Editorial Change 1 (October 2024); the Document Control page footer reads 'July 2024 / October 2021', probably an artefact of the change, while other pages say 'July 2021'. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate cover pages. The extraction has 53 PDF pages (registry: 52); the last page is blank. Several internal cross-references are wrong in the source: 4.1 says the Pseudo-Randomizer is 'defined in section 5' (it is section 6); B3 places the LDPC codes in 'section 5' (they are in section 4); Annex D's note says normative references are 'listed in 1.6.3' (they are in 1.7); the CLTU reception tables are called 'tables 5-1 and 5-2' in the text but listed as Tables 5-3 and 5-4 in the contents. Normative references still cite TC SDLP issue 3 (2015) and USLP issue 1 (2018). Section 1.7 references 'constitute provisions of this Recommended Standard' (kind 'normative'); Annex D lists informative references. No individual authors are named.
